Method 1 check: the flux from a cylindrical Lambertian surface per unit length is F = πL·πD = π²·(L·D), so I′ = LD = 3 000/π² ≈ 304 cd/m. Seen from angle α, the projected area of an element is D·dx·cosα, with r = h/cosα and dx = h·dα/cos²α. This gives dE_h = I′cos²α·dα/h. Integrating from −π/2 to π/2 gives E_h = πI′/(2h) = 3 000/(6π) = 159.15 lx.

Method 2 check: by translation and rotational symmetry, 3 000 lm per metre is distributed uniformly over a coaxial cylinder of radius h, whose area per metre is 2πh. Directly below the source, the cylinder normal and the floor normal coincide, so E_h = 3 000/(2π×3) = 159.15 lx. Both methods agree, so option (4) is correct.
